name: Why does my remodeled room feel glaring even though the lights are attractive?

mainEntity.name: Why does my remodeled room feel glaring even though the lights are attractive?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Glare usually comes from excessive brightness, exposed light sources, reflective surfaces, poor aiming, or fixtures placed where occupants look directly into them. Adding more fixtures without correcting the source can make the room brighter but less comfortable.

**Context:** Polished countertops, mirrors, glossy floors, screens, and light-colored walls can amplify reflected glare. Diffusers, shielding, lower-output products, indirect light, and better placement may solve the problem more effectively.

**Key factors:**
- Fixture angle, trim, and beam spread
- Surface reflectivity and viewing direction
- Dimming range and source brightness
- Seating, work surfaces, and screen locations

**Practical guidance:** Identify exactly when and where glare occurs, then test a sample fixture or trim from normal eye level. Keep accent fixtures aimed away from screens and avoid placing bright sources directly in the usual line of sight.

Elite Remodeling & Design can adjust lighting placement and finish coordination during design development.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attractive fixtures can still glare when the source is exposed, too bright, poorly aimed, or reflected by counters, mirrors, floors, or screens. Test from normal eye level, use dimming or diffusion, and adjust placement before adding more fixtures. Document where glare appears during daily activities.
